findings.requirement: A record is approved by the judge cascade: JEV above 0.9 fast-tracks it, else the judge model asks through the question tool and JEV judges again
findings.what: Check 4, contradictory bar for a model approval. Example 4 approves SR-185 by auto-model (haiku) at confidence 0.8, but the second requirement's example 9 refuses a by: auto-model entry at 0.6 'under the cascade's 0.9 floor', and DEC-089 speaks of 'the 0.9 minimum'. 0.8 is under 0.9, so the file approves and refuses the same kind of entry. The drop reason for SR-191/EX-5 ('give way to the cascade's 0.9 floor') has the same problem, so the behaviour 'a model verdict below the bar approves nothing' (SR-191/EX-5 and EX-6, 10 linked tests on SR-191) now has no stated bar. State one rule: either a model approval needs confidence at or above a named bar (then example 4 must change), or the model's 'clear' needs no number (then example 9 and DEC-089 must not cite 0.9 for auto-model). Also say whether a model 'clear' after the owner's answers approves when the fast track is off (assumption 2 says approval then rests on the owner's answers).

findings.requirement: A record is approved by the judge cascade: JEV above 0.9 fast-tracks it, else the judge model asks through the question tool and JEV judges again
findings.what: Check 3, several behaviours under one title, and the statement does not match its examples. (a) The cascade itself (examples 1 to 5). (b) Nothing approves from tests, links or consistency, and /plumb settle is gone (examples 6, 7): a removal, not the cascade. (c) Recovery of an older record's words from past transcripts (examples 8 to 11, from SR-118): the statement never mentions it, and it is the legacy repair of INT-032's 'Recover the quotes' (records whose words plumb never logged), so it reads as a one-off migration dressed as a behaviour. Under v2 every record has a pre-intent (P3), so either make it its own requirement with a statement, or drop it as a one-off. (d) Examples 12 and 13 restate behaviour other drafts own: round limit then debug workflow is P5's example 1 (judge cascade past its round limit), and 'no judge can be reached' is P8's no-judge requirement (key missing, fast track would run). Keep one owner for each.

findings.requirement: Only the owner switches the fast track; every judge approval is marked, counted and undone on the owner's word
findings.what: Check 3, four behaviours under one title: (a) only the owner switches the fast track (examples 1 to 4, 10); (b) a JEV version change suspends it (examples 5, 6); (c) a judge approval is marked, counted in the turn-end line and undone by the owner's words (examples 7, 8); (d) an approval entry below the bar is inert and reported by validate (example 9, DEC-089, a validation guard). Example 7 duplicates P3's example on reversing a judge approval by speaking ('the reminder rule you approved is wrong', no command or id), and P4 owns the calibration-label side of a reversal (reversed as misread or as intent change), which the third requirement's example 5 repeats. Split (a)/(b) from (c)/(d) and keep each reversal rule in one draft.

Example 12: 'the case goes to the debug workflow, which asks the owner only in last resort' is not observable in one case; say 'a debug workflow opens, the agent is told in one line, the owner is not asked' (as P5 does), and the given never states the round limit (the intent assumption says three by default, a setting): put the number in the given. Second requirement, example 7: 'INT-030 is proposed again and goes back through the loop' (same defect found in P3's draft); say that the cascade judges it again and what the owner sees.

findings.what: Check 2/1, a silently dropped guard. SR-041 ('Never for ... a set member, an edit of an owner-confirmed record') and the confirmed INT-017 wont ('Auto-approve ... an edit of a record you confirmed') are not carried and not listed as dropped. The drafted first requirement approves any proposed intent, requirement or decision, so a reworded or changed owner-confirmed record could be fast-tracked, although P3 keeps the owner as arbiter of anything that 'changes older intent'. Add a guard (an edit that changes a confirmed record's meaning goes to the owner's arbitration, P3) with an example, or list the guard as dropped with the P3 reason. Refutation tried: P3's first requirement sends an edit 'back to the judge', which covers a pure rewording but not a change of confirmed meaning.
